title: JUCE VST Plugin Development Playbook
description: End-to-end development playbook for building creative unique VST audio plugins with JUCE and AI assistance. Covers the full plugin lifecycle from concept through release: spec development, DSP architecture, implementation, GUI, testing, DAW validation, optimization, and release. Designed for a single developer retaining full creative control with AI handling code generation, review, and validation. Each phase is gated — nothing advances until acceptance criteria are met.
extracted_from: conversation_full.md — single 24,292-line session (2026-03-27 to 2026-03-28) building Epiphany Machine VST v3

roles.you: Creative director, sound designer, final decision-maker on all audio/UX choices. You define WHAT the plugin does and HOW it should sound.
roles.ai: Code architect, implementation engine, reviewer, test generator. AI handles HOW to build what you've defined. Never makes creative decisions autonomously.

superpowers_mapping.brainstorming: Use in Phase 0 to develop the plugin concept and spec. Session 1 used this: AI asked multi-choice questions, user picked options, iterated until design was locked.
superpowers_mapping.writing_plans: Use in Phase 2 to produce the architecture doc and task breakdown. Session 2 used this to generate a 1577-line implementation plan.
superpowers_mapping.executing_plans: Use in Phases 3-7 to implement each task from the plan. Session 3-5 used subagent-driven-development (fresh agent per task + two-stage review).
superpowers_mapping.subagent_driven_development: Preferred over executing-plans for implementation. Dispatches one fresh subagent per task with two-stage review (spec compliance then code quality). Caught critical bugs the implementer missed.

integration_notes.juce_docs: Feed JUCE module docs as context for the relevant phase (juce_dsp for DSP phase, juce_gui_basics for GUI phase, juce_audio_processors for integration phase)
integration_notes.session_history: After each completed phase, extract the working conversation into a phase summary. This becomes the context seed for the next phase — prevents token waste from carrying full history.

checklists.title: Phase 0: Plugin Concept & Spec
checklists.purpose: Define exactly what you're building before writing any code. The AI should be ASKING YOU questions here, not proposing solutions. This phase produces the spec that drives everything else.
checklists.actual_workflow_observed: User provided v2 spec + problem statement ('effect not noticeable enough'). AI used brainstorming skill to ask multiple-choice questions about each design dimension. User picked options (a/b/c/d) for each. 12 design questions answered interactively. Design took ~35 minutes.

items.title: Define plugin type and signal flow
items.description:
AI should prompt you for each decision:
- Plugin type: Synthesizer, effect, analyzer, or hybrid?
- Signal flow: mono/stereo in, mono/stereo out? Sidechain input?
- DSP chain: what processing blocks exist and in what order?
- Parameter count estimate: how many knobs/sliders/switches?

From session: User defined signal flow as Input → TextureBodyDetector → GlitchEngine → MORPH blend → FDN → Feedback loop (PitchDrifter → DualFilter → Wavefolder → soft clip) → DualFilter → MIX → tanh() → Output
items.session_evidence: Session 1: User answered 12 multi-choice questions to define signal flow, chose 8-line FDN, wavefolder+filter-in-feedback, adaptive grain envelopes, per-line pan replacing StereoWidener

items.title: Define the sound identity
items.description:
What should this plugin SOUND like? Reference existing plugins, genre context, character words.

From session: User said 'make it very intense', 'capable of producing wild harsh sounds if desired', 'more abstract ambient psychedelic sound', 'weird and interesting but tolerable by human listeners'. These exact words drove every DSP decision.
items.session_evidence: Session 1: 'the effect is not nearly noticeable enough. it should be capable of producing wild harsh sounds if desired... more abstract ambient psychedelic sound capabilities'

items.title: Define technical constraints
items.description:
Lock down: JUCE version, target formats, target OS, DAWs for validation, sample rates, buffer sizes, CPU budget.

From session: JUCE 7.0.12, C++17, VST3, CMake build, Linux, support 44.1k-192kHz
items.session_evidence: Session 1-2: JUCE 7.0.12 identified from build deps, C++17 standard, CMake build system, Linux target

items.title: Gain staging design
items.description:
CRITICAL — from session: User said 'don't make it run too hot, but we want the effect to be intense. without drive the effect shouldn't be overly hot though.' This became the design principle: drive is opt-in intensity, wavefolder output normalized by /foldAmount to add complexity without volume.

AI should identify existing gain staging issues before proposing solutions. In session: 6 layers of conservative gain staging were identified as the root cause of 'not noticeable enough'.
items.session_evidence: Session 1: Identified -6dB FDN output cut, 0.95 decay multiplier, StereoWidener soft clip, 8kHz feedback LPF, double freeze soft clip, tame Q ranges — all compounding to make effect barely audible

AI will suggest generic names. REJECT THEM. User must define the creative direction.

From session: AI proposed 'Superposition, Entanglement, Dark Matter' — user rejected: 'make all the names more creative, dont use your default assumptions, because there are other effects with these names as i told you to do this already.' AI revised to more unique names.
items.session_evidence: Session 1: User corrected preset names from generic to creative quantum physics theme with unique names like 'Both States Neither State', 'Spooky Geometry', 'The Invisible 96%'

items.description:

From session: Spec written to docs/superpowers/specs/ — included signal flow diagram, parameter list with ranges, gain staging removals, new values, preset list. Three self-review issues found and fixed before user approval.

checklists.title: Phase 1: Performance Audit (pre-implementation)
checklists.purpose: Before ANY new features, audit the existing codebase for memory/CPU/thread-safety issues. User explicitly requested this: 'before building this we will need to have you analyze the project fully for memory and cpu use improvements to make sure it runs lean but do not impact sound or design'.

items.title: Thread safety audit
items.description:
Scan for non-atomic shared state between audio and GUI threads.

From session: Found `bool systemChanging` in PresetManager — non-atomic bool shared between threads. Fixed to `std::atomic<bool> systemChanging{false}`.
items.session_evidence: Session 3, Task 0 Fix 1: PresetManager.h systemChanging changed to std::atomic<bool>
items.validation: Build succeeds, no thread sanitizer warnings

items.title: Instance isolation audit
items.description:
Check for static variables shared across plugin instances.

From session: Found `static int lastPreset` in PluginProcessor.cpp — shared across all instances. Fixed to instance member `int lastPresetIdx = 0`.
items.session_evidence: Session 3, Task 0 Fix 2: Moved from static to member variable in PluginProcessor.h
items.validation: Multiple instances don't interfere with each other's preset state

items.title: Audio thread allocation audit
items.description:
Search for heap allocations or large memsets on the audio thread.

From session: GlitchEngine had silence gate that cleared 1MB buffer (131072 * 2 channels * 4 bytes) on audio thread when signal dropped below -80dBFS. Fix: remove silence gate entirely.
items.session_evidence: Session 3, Task 0 Fix 3: Removed kSilenceThreshold, inputPeak, silenceCount, isSilent from GlitchEngine
items.validation: No large memory operations in processBlock path

items.title: Parameter lookup optimization
items.description:
Check for O(N) parameter lookups on the audio thread.

From session: PresetManager.applyInterpolated() did per-block linear search through all parameters for each parameter write. Fixed with O(1) cache using vector-of-pairs keyed on parameter ID strings.

CRITICAL LESSON: First fix attempt keyed cache on parameter NAMES (via getName(256)) but idx() lambda still called getParameter(id) — an O(N) scan — before hitting the cache. Spec reviewer caught this. Second fix keyed on parameter ID strings directly with no intermediary getParameter() call.
items.session_evidence: Session 3, Task 0 Fix 4: Two rounds — first commit keyed on names (still O(N)), spec reviewer caught it, fix subagent re-keyed on IDs (true O(1)). Commits 392e2d8 then 52cf7d7.
items.validation: paramIndexCache.find(std::string(id)) with no getParameter() call in hot path

gate_conditions: No non-atomic shared state between audio/GUI threads

No heap allocations in processBlock path

Build succeeds with all fixes

checklists.title: Phase 4: Core DSP Implementation
checklists.purpose: Build the audio engine module by module. Two-stage review after each. You compile and LISTEN after each significant block.

items.title: Implement DSP modules (iterate per task list)
items.description:
For EACH DSP module:
1. Dispatch implementer subagent with task spec + relevant source files
2. Dispatch spec compliance reviewer (does it match the plan?)
3. Dispatch code quality reviewer (is it correct DSP? thread-safe? performant?)
4. If issues found: dispatch fix subagent, then re-review BOTH stages
5. Build and verify compilation

CRITICAL: The code quality reviewer catches things the spec reviewer misses. Do NOT skip it.

From session: Code quality reviewer caught 3 critical bugs the implementer missed:
- DiffusionNetwork: Hadamard not in feedback path (8 independent combs, not FDN)
- DiffusionNetwork: Buffer overflow at >48kHz (kBufSize=4096 too small for 192kHz)
- GlitchEngine: Reverse playback formula off-by-one + no grainSpeed in reverse

And the plan itself had an error:
- DualFilter: Q constant 24.5f gives Q_max=25, not 50 as spec requires. Corrected to 49.5f.

items.title: Diagnose and fix reported issues
items.description:
Read processBlock, trace the signal flow, identify root causes.

From session, three bugs found and fixed:

1. DRIVE KNOB INERT (critical): driveSmoothed.getNextValue() was never called in the per-sample loop. Without getNextValue(), SmoothedValue never advances from initial value (0.0). Wavefolder was permanently bypassed (drive > 0.001f check always false). Fix: add driveSmoothed.getNextValue() in Step 4's per-sample loop.

PREVENTION RULE: After implementing processBlock, audit EVERY SmoothedValue — verify each one has getNextValue() called per-sample in the normal audio path. getCurrentValue() alone does NOT advance the smoother.

2. MIX RANGE COMPRESSED: Linear blend dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix concentrates audible change in low end. FDN output louder than dry signal compounds this. Fix: switch to equal-power mixing using cos(mix * PI/2) for dry and sin(mix * PI/2) for wet.

PREVENTION RULE: Always use equal-power (cosine) dry/wet mixing, not linear.

3. CONTROLS PERCEIVED DELAYED: Changing density/chaos/morph only affects new FDN input; existing reverb tail persists at old character for full decay duration. With 4.0s default decay, user waits ~4 seconds to hear changes. Fix: lower default decay from 4.0s to 2.0s.

PREVENTION RULE: Default decay parameter should be short enough that parameter changes are audible within ~2 seconds. User can always increase it.
items.session_evidence: Session 6: All three fixes in commit 8326bc3

juce_patterns.description: Every reusable JUCE API pattern extracted from the session history.

gotchas: NormalisableRange skew parameter: 0.5 for frequency-like params (decay, feedback), 0.3 for cutoff frequencies
AudioParameterChoice stores values as 0-based index integers, not strings
Parameter ranges must be consistent between APVTS definition, PresetData values, and DSP code

smoothed_values.critical_rule: EVERY SmoothedValue MUST have getNextValue() called per-sample in processBlock. getCurrentValue() alone does NOT advance the smoother — the value stays stuck at initial.
gotchas: If you only call getCurrentValue() without getNextValue(), the smoother never advances from its initial value. This was a CRITICAL BUG in session — driveSmoothed was stuck at 0.0 forever.
Call setTargetValue() once per block (before the sample loop), getNextValue() per sample (inside the loop)
For parameters read later in the block (not in the main per-sample loop), you can advance with getNextValue() in one loop and read with getCurrentValue() later — but the advance MUST happen
smoothed_values.session_source: Session 6: driveSmoothed bug — getNextValue() never called, drive permanently zero. Commit 8326bc3

gotchas: Attachment must be stored as unique_ptr member — if it goes out of scope, the connection breaks
Never manually sync slider values to parameters — the attachment handles everything

dsp_module_lifecycle.pattern: Standard prepare/reset/process lifecycle for DSP modules
rules: prepare(): allocate buffers, compute coefficients, set sample rate
reset(): zero all state (delay lines, LPF states, LFO phases)
process(): in-place stereo processing, no allocations
All modules must handle sample rate changes correctly in prepare()
dsp_module_lifecycle.session_source: Session 3-5: All DSP modules (DiffusionNetwork, GlitchEngine, DualFilter, PitchDrifter, TextureBodyDetector) follow this pattern

knob_group.pattern: Reusable KnobGroup struct wrapping slider + label + value label + attachment
knob_group.code_pattern: struct KnobGroup { Slider slider; Label label; Label valueLabel; unique_ptr<SliderAttachment> attach; void setup(...); void place(x,y,sz,...); }

look_and_feel.pattern: Custom LookAndFeel_V4 subclass for consistent visual style
rules: Apply to top-level editor — cascades to children

timer_updates.pattern: Timer-based GUI updates for meters/value labels
timer_updates.code_pattern: class Editor : public AudioProcessorEditor, private Timer { void timerCallback() override { updateValueLabels(); } };
timer_updates.session_source: Session 4-5: PluginEditor inherits juce::Timer for value label updates

gotchas: Verify arithmetic: account for ALL offsets between parent container Y and component Y
From session: fbPanelH=160 didn't account for 12px offset between fbPanelY and fbTop, causing drive label to overflow

rules: No heap allocations (new, malloc, std::vector resize)
Use juce::ScopedNoDenormals at top of processBlock
Use std::atomic<bool> for flags shared between threads (not plain bool)
Pre-allocate all buffers in prepareToPlay, not in processBlock
Use juce::SmoothedValue for parameter changes (no raw parameter reads that cause zipper noise)
gotchas: From session: std::unordered_map.find() can allocate due to std::string construction. Use std::vector<std::pair<>> for audio-thread lookups.
From session: GlitchEngine silence gate cleared 1MB buffer on audio thread. Large memsets are allocations in disguise.
audio_thread_safety.session_source: Session 3: Task 0 performance audit identified multiple audio-thread safety violations

equal_power_mix.formula: dryGain = cos(mix * PI/2); wetGain = sin(mix * PI/2);
equal_power_mix.why: Linear blend (dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix) concentrates audible change in low end of range. Equal-power keeps perceived level constant across full sweep.
equal_power_mix.session_source: Session 6: Mix knob bug — linear blend only effective in first 30% of range. Fixed with cosine mixing.

dsp_catalog.name: DiffusionNetwork
dsp_catalog.algorithm: 8-line FDN with Fast Hadamard Transform (FHT) mixing in feedback path

decaySeconds.note: RT60 time. Originally defaulted to 4.0 but lowered to 2.0 because long tail masked parameter changes

damping.note: One-pole LPF on feedback, multiplied by (1 - dampMute) during freeze

freeze.note: Smoothly gates input, boosts feedback to 0.999, mutes damping

implementation.buffer_size_note: Originally 4096, overflowed at 96kHz+. Longest delay at 192kHz = 14044 samples.
implementation.process_structure: 3-pass per sample: (1) read+fbGain+LPF, (2) hadamardMix in feedback, (3) write mixed+input. Output uses post-FHT taps with panning.

dsp_catalog.cpu_cost: Moderate — 8 delay reads/writes + 3-stage FHT per sample. RT60 gains pre-computed per block (was per-sample, fixed).
known_issues: CRITICAL (fixed): FHT was originally at output only, not in feedback path — produced 8 independent combs, not FDN
IMPORTANT (fixed): pow(10,...) computed per-line per-sample — moved to per-block pre-computation
MINOR (fixed): isFrozen member was dead state — removed

dsp_catalog.name: GlitchEngine
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Circular-buffer grain playback with chaos-driven selection, adaptive envelopes, and pitch drift

drift.note: Random ±drift semitones per grain via pow(2, randomSt/12)

implementation.grain_playback: Float readPos with linear interpolation, grainSpeed for pitch
implementation.drift_guard: if (drift > 0.0f && !grainReverse) — drift disabled on reverse grains to prevent out-of-window reads

dsp_catalog.sample_rate_handling: prepare(sr, spb) stores sample rate for grain length calculations
dsp_catalog.cpu_cost: Low-moderate — one grain active at a time, linear interpolation per sample
known_issues: CRITICAL (fixed): Reverse playback formula off-by-one — (grainStart+grainLength-consumed) reads past grain end on first sample
CRITICAL (fixed): writeHead unbounded overflow — needed & kBufMask
IMPORTANT (fixed): Drift applied to reverse grains caused out-of-window reads
REMOVED: Silence gate (-80dBFS) cleared 1MB buffer on audio thread

dsp_catalog.name: DualFilter
dsp_catalog.type: Dual Cytomic TPT State Variable Filter
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Two independent Cytomic SVFs (texture + body paths) with LFO modulation

implementation.q_mapping: K = 1.0f / (0.5f + reso * 49.5f) — gives Q range 0.5 to 50
implementation.q_mapping_note: Originally 24.5f (Q max=25). Plan had math error. Corrected to 49.5f for Q max=50.
implementation.lfo_depth: modCut = texCutoff * pow(2, lfoVal * lfoDepth * 3.0f) — ±3 octaves

dsp_catalog.cpu_cost: Low — two SVF updates per sample
known_issues: IMPORTANT (fixed): Q constant 24.5f gives Q_max=25, not 50. Plan had math error. Corrected to 49.5f.

dsp_catalog.name: PitchDrifter
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Two overlapping grains with Hann windows, playback rate from pitch ratio

drift.note: Mapped from DRIFT parameter, applied in feedback loop only

dsp_catalog.cpu_cost: Low — two grain reads per sample with interpolation
dsp_catalog.session_source: Session 2: Spec defined, minimal changes in v3

dsp_catalog.name: TextureBodyDetector
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Splits signal into texture (transients) and body (sustained) components

glitchFocus.note: Routes more texture vs body to glitch engine

dsp_catalog.session_source: Session 2: Spec defined, no changes in v3

dsp_catalog.name: Wavefolder
dsp_catalog.algorithm: output = input + drive * (sin(input * foldAmt * PI) / foldAmt - input)

drive.note: True bypass at drive=0 due to crossfade formula

implementation.inline: Implemented inline in processBlock, not a separate class

dsp_catalog.cpu_cost: Low — one sin() per sample when drive > 0
known_issues: IMPORTANT (fixed): foldAmt multiplier was 3.0 instead of spec's 4.0
DESIGN: Original spec formula sin(x*PI)/1.0 at drive=0 amplifies by PI. Fixed with crossfade: output = input + drive * (folded - input)

failure_modes.description: Every bug hit during development, indexed by phase, with prevention rules that become checklist items.

bugs.symptom: O(1) cache optimization still had O(N) parameter lookup
bugs.root_cause: Cache keyed on parameter names (via getName(256)) but idx() lambda still called getParameter(id) — itself O(N) — before hitting cache
bugs.fix: Re-key cache on parameter ID strings; idx() uses pure paramIndexCache.find(std::string(id)) with no getParameter() call
bugs.prevention_rule: When optimizing lookups, verify the ENTIRE call chain is O(1). A cache that requires O(N) to compute its key is not a cache.

bugs.root_cause: Haiku model over-eagerly added commented-out StereoWidener references in PluginProcessor files that were Task 8-9 scope
bugs.prevention_rule: In subagent prompts, explicitly list which files are in-scope AND state 'Do not modify any other files'. Lower-capability models (haiku) are more prone to scope creep.

bugs.symptom: FDN produces slapback echo character instead of diffuse reverb
bugs.root_cause: Hadamard Transform applied only to output summation, not in feedback path. Delay lines have no cross-coupling in feedback — they're 8 independent recirculating delays.
bugs.fix: Restructured process() into 3 passes: read+fbGain+LPF → hadamardMix(feedback) → write mixed+input back to delay lines
bugs.prevention_rule: In any FDN implementation, verify the mixing matrix is in the FEEDBACK path. If it's only at the output, the delay lines are independent combs, not an FDN. This is the most common FDN implementation error.

bugs.symptom: Audio corruption at sample rates above 48kHz
bugs.root_cause: kBufSize=4096 too small. Longest delay (base 3511) at 96kHz = 7022 samples, at 192kHz = 14044. The & kBufMask wrap silently reads/writes wrong positions.
bugs.prevention_rule: Always compute maximum delay length at highest supported sample rate: max_delay = max_base_length * (max_sr / base_sr). Buffer must be at least this large. Use power-of-2 for & mask optimization.

bugs.symptom: Reverse grain playback reads past grain boundary on first sample
bugs.root_cause: Original formula (grainStart+grainLength-consumed) at consumed=0 gives grainStart+grainLength, which is ONE PAST the end of the grain buffer
bugs.prevention_rule: Reverse playback formulas must use (start + length - 1) as the starting position, not (start + length). Always verify the first and last sample positions are within bounds.
All circular buffer indices must use & mask or % modulo wrapping.

bugs.symptom: Drift on reverse grains reads outside grain window
bugs.root_cause: Grain speed modification changes playback rate, but reverse grains count DOWN through the buffer. Modified speed causes read position to land outside the grain's buffer region.
bugs.fix: Guard: if (drift > 0.0f && !grainReverse) — only apply drift to forward grains
bugs.prevention_rule: When modifying grain playback speed, verify bounds for both forward and reverse playback modes separately.

bugs.symptom: Filter Q range only reaches 25 instead of spec's 50
bugs.root_cause: Plan specified K = 1/(0.5 + reso*24.5f). At reso=1: K=1/25=0.04, Q=1/(2*K)=12.5. The plan's math was wrong — need K=1/(0.5+reso*49.5f) to get Q=50.
bugs.prevention_rule: Verify filter Q mapping math: for Cytomic SVF, Q = 1/(2*K). If target Q_max is X, then K_min = 1/(2*X), so constant = (1/K_min - 0.5). Always compute K at reso=1.0 and verify Q matches spec.
bugs.caught_by: Code quality reviewer (caught that 24.5f gives Q=25, not 50)

bugs.root_cause: Code used 1.0f + drive * 3.0f for foldAmt, spec says 1.0f + drive * 4.0f (foldAmt=5 at drive=1)
bugs.prevention_rule: When implementing formulas from spec, copy constants exactly. Don't round or approximate.

bugs.symptom: Feedback path can go unstable without protection
bugs.root_cause: Spec calls for x/(1+|x|) soft-clip at end of feedback chain. Implementer omitted it.
bugs.fix: Added soft-clip loop after wavefolder: fbL[i] = fbL[i] / (1.0f + std::abs(fbL[i]))
bugs.prevention_rule: Every feedback loop MUST have a safety limiter. Check: does the feedback path have a final soft-clip or hard-clip before feeding back?

bugs.root_cause: getTailLengthSeconds() returned 8.0 but decay parameter goes up to 20.0 seconds
bugs.prevention_rule: getTailLengthSeconds() must return the MAXIMUM possible tail length, which is the max value of the decay parameter.

bugs.symptom: Drive value label renders below feedback panel border
bugs.root_cause: Plan computed fbPanelH=160 but didn't account for 12px offset between fbPanelY (col2.getY()+158) and fbTop (col2.getY()+170). Drive label at fbTop+ks+28+12 = fbPanelY+170-158+ks+40 > 160.
bugs.prevention_rule: When computing panel heights, account for ALL Y-offsets between the panel origin and the component origin. Walk the arithmetic: panel starts at panelY, component starts at componentY, component bottom = componentY + componentHeight. Verify componentBottom - panelY <= panelHeight.

bugs.symptom: DRIVE knob has absolutely zero effect on audio
bugs.root_cause: driveSmoothed initialized with setCurrentAndTargetValue(0.0). Each processBlock calls setTargetValue(getV('drive')). But getNextValue() was never called in the per-sample loop — only getCurrentValue() in Step 10. Without getNextValue(), SmoothedValue never advances from 0.0. The wavefolder check (drive > 0.001f) was always false.
bugs.fix: Added driveSmoothed.getNextValue() in Step 4's per-sample loop (consistent with how feedbackSmoothed is advanced there)
bugs.prevention_rule: AFTER IMPLEMENTING PROCESSBLOCK: Audit every SmoothedValue declaration. For each one, grep for getNextValue() in the per-sample loop. If missing, the parameter is DEAD. This is a silent bug — no crash, no error, just a permanently inert control.
bugs.caught_by: User (DAW testing) — NOT caught by ANY reviewer

bugs.symptom: Mix knob only effective in first ~30% of range
bugs.root_cause: Linear blend dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix concentrates audible change in low end. FDN output louder than dry signal compounds this — even small mix values sound very wet.
bugs.fix: Switched to equal-power mixing: dryGain = cos(mix * PI/2), wetGain = sin(mix * PI/2)
bugs.prevention_rule: ALWAYS use equal-power (cosine) dry/wet mixing, not linear. Linear is perceptually wrong for audio mixing.

bugs.symptom: Parameter changes feel delayed — no immediate audible response
bugs.root_cause: Changing density/chaos/morph only affects NEW input to FDN. Existing reverb tail persists at old character for full decay duration. With default decay at 4.0s, user waits ~4 seconds to hear any change.
bugs.prevention_rule: Default decay/tail parameter should be 2s or less so parameter changes are audible quickly. Long decay is available but shouldn't be the default for first impressions.

bugs.root_cause: Remote had 4 commits not present locally
bugs.fix: git pull → resolve merge conflicts on .so binary → push
bugs.prevention_rule: Before pushing a large batch of local commits, always git pull first. For binary files in merge conflicts, use 'git checkout --ours' or '--theirs' explicitly.

session_management.description: When to start fresh sessions, what context to carry forward, and what to drop. Extracted from 6 session boundaries observed.

session_boundaries_observed.trigger: Context limit (brainstorming complete, spec writing started)
session_boundaries_observed.context_carried: Full design decisions, signal flow, parameter list, preset names, gain staging philosophy, spec file path
session_boundaries_observed.context_dropped: Multi-choice discussion transcript, intermediate design options that were rejected

session_boundaries_observed.trigger: Context limit + API 529 errors during plan writing
session_boundaries_observed.context_carried: Spec file path, plan file path, all 25 source file contents (summarized), task list
session_boundaries_observed.context_dropped: Full source file contents (too large), API error retry transcript

session_boundaries_observed.context_carried: Plan file path, task progress (Task 0 complete), commit hashes, pending tasks list, all file modifications and review results
All completed task commits, pending Task 9 fixes (specific issues), remaining tasks (10, 11)

session_boundaries_observed.trigger: All implementation complete, user testing begins
session_boundaries_observed.context_carried: Final git log with all commits, v3.0.0 tag, install path, manual smoke test checklist
session_boundaries_observed.context_dropped: All implementation details — code is committed, review is done

when_to_start_fresh: After completing a phase gate (spec approved, plan approved, DSP done, etc.)
When context limit is approaching (Claude starts losing earlier decisions)
After implementing 3-4 tasks — context accumulates fast with subagent transcripts
When switching from implementation to user testing (different workflow entirely)
When API errors (529) indicate context is too large
what_to_carry_forward: Spec file path and key decisions
Plan file path and task progress (which tasks are done, which are pending)
Specific pending issues with exact symptoms and proposed fixes
what_to_drop: Full source file contents (AI can re-read them)
Subagent dispatch/review transcripts (decisions are in commits)
Intermediate design options that were rejected
Multi-choice discussion transcripts (decisions are in spec)
rules.compaction_strategy: Use /compact when context is filling up. The auto-generated summary captures: primary request, key technical concepts, files modified, errors and fixes, pending tasks, current work. This is sufficient to continue seamlessly.

cost_optimization.description: Context window budget allocation based on observed token usage patterns.

model_selection.opus: Use for brainstorming (Phase 0) and complex architectural decisions. Session 1 used Opus.
model_selection.sonnet: Use for plan writing and implementation execution. Sessions 2-6 switched to Sonnet after API 529 errors on Opus. Sonnet was reliable and sufficient for all implementation tasks.
model_selection.haiku: Use ONLY for simple, well-constrained tasks. Session 4 used Haiku for Task 1 (CMakeLists update) — it went out of scope and modified files it shouldn't have. Higher-capability models are more reliable for scoped work.

context_budget.spec_as_context: ~2000 tokens. Keep it concise. The spec is the authoritative reference — paste it at session start.
context_budget.plan_as_context: ~5000 tokens for the full plan. For task-level work, paste only the current task's section (~300-500 tokens).
context_budget.source_files: Let AI read them fresh each session rather than carrying file contents in context. Saves ~3000-5000 tokens per session.
context_budget.subagent_transcripts: These consume the most context. Each implement+review cycle adds ~3000-5000 tokens. After 3-4 tasks, start a fresh session.
context_budget.compaction_summaries: ~1000-2000 tokens each. These are efficient — carry full state in compressed form.

patterns_that_waste_tokens: Carrying full source files in context instead of letting AI re-read them
Retrying after API 529 errors in the same session — start fresh instead
Asking AI 'what should we do next?' when the plan already exists — just paste the next task
Full conversation history across sessions — use compaction summaries
patterns_that_save_tokens: One task per subagent dispatch — clean context, focused work
Spec + current task section as context — AI doesn't need the whole plan
Let AI re-read files instead of pasting them — files may have changed
Use /compact when context fills — auto-generated summary is efficient
Switch to Sonnet for implementation — reliable and lower cost than Opus

how_to_run_this: 1. Start a new session with Opus. Paste Phase 0 + brainstorming skill. AI asks questions, you answer. Output: spec doc.
2. New session with Sonnet. Paste spec + Phase 2 + writing-plans skill. Output: task-level plan with code.
3. New session. Run Phase 1 (perf audit) if upgrading existing code. Paste plan Task 0.
4. For Phases 3-7: one session per 3-4 tasks. Use subagent-driven-development. Paste: spec + current task section from plan.
5. At each phase gate, review all conditions. If a condition isn't met, fix before advancing.
6. Phase 9: Load in DAW and LISTEN. Report what you hear. AI diagnoses and fixes.
7. After each session, save key output. Compaction summaries carry state automatically.
when_to_break_sessions: After 3-4 implementation tasks (subagent transcripts fill context)
When API 529 errors occur (context too large for model)
When switching from implementation to DAW testing

juce_reference_context.description: Feed these JUCE module docs as context to the AI for the relevant phase.
